title: Proposition 3.1.4 (The Units Form a Group)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. Then \(R^{\times}\) , the set of units of \(R\) , is an abelian group under the multiplication of \(R\) , with identity \(1\) , and the inverse of \(u\) in this group is \(u^{-1}\) .

title: Theorem 3.1.1 (Basic Properties of Groups)
content: Let \(G\) be a group and \(a, b, c \in G\) . The identity element of \(G\) is unique. The inverse of \(a\) is unique. We denote it by \(a^{-1}\) . \((a^{-1})^{-1} = a\) and \((ab)^{-1} = b^{-1}a^{-1}\) . (Cancellation) If \(ab = ac\) , then \(b = c\) . If \(ba = ca\) , then \(b = c\) . The equations \(ax = b\) and \(ya = b\) have exactly one solution \(x \in G\) and exactly one solution \(y \in G\) : \(x = a^{-1}b\) and \(y = ba^{-1}\) .

title: Definition 3.2.1 (Subgroup)
page: 3.2 Subgroups and the Subgroups of the Integers
content: Let \(G\) be a group. A subset \(H \subseteq G\) is a subgroup of \(G\) if \(e \in H\) , and \(ab \in H\) and \(a^{-1} \in H\) for all \(a, b \in H\) .

title: Definition 3.2.2 (Subgroup Generated by an Element)
page: 3.2 Subgroups and the Subgroups of the Integers
content: Let \(G\) be a group and \(g \in G\) . The subgroup generated by \(g\) is \[ \langle g \rangle \coloneqq \{ g^n : n \in \nZ \} , \] with the powers of @def-group-integer-power . In additive notation, \(\langle a \rangle = \{ n \cdot a : n \in \nZ \}\) .

title: Definition 3.3.1 (Group Homomorphism)
content: Let \(G\) and \(H\) be groups. A function \(\varphi \colon G \to H\) is a homomorphism if \(\varphi(ab) = \varphi(a)\varphi(b)\) for all \(a, b \in G\) . A bijective homomorphism is an isomorphism . The groups \(G\) and \(H\) are isomorphic , written \(G \cong H\) , if there exists an isomorphism \(G \to H\) . The kernel of \(\varphi\) is \[ \ker \varphi \coloneqq \{ g \in G : \varphi(g) = e_H \} , \] where \(e_H\) is the identity of \(H\) .

title: Proposition 3.3.2 (Composites and Inverses of Homomorphisms)
content: Let \(G\) , \(H\) and \(K\) be groups. If \(\varphi \colon G \to H\) and \(\psi \colon H \to K\) are homomorphisms, then so is \(\psi \circ \varphi \colon G \to K\) . If \(\varphi \colon G \to H\) is an isomorphism, then its inverse function \(\varphi^{-1} \colon H \to G\) is an isomorphism. \(\id_G\) is an isomorphism. Consequently \(G \cong G\) ; if \(G \cong H\) , then \(H \cong G\) ; and if \(G \cong H\) and \(H \cong K\) , then \(G \cong K\) .

title: Proposition 3.3.3 (Injective Exactly When the Kernel Is Trivial)
content: A homomorphism \(\varphi \colon G \to H\) is injective if and only if \(\ker \varphi = \{e_G\}\) .

title: Theorem 3.3.1 (Basic Properties of Homomorphisms)
content: Let \(\varphi \colon G \to H\) be a homomorphism of groups, and let \(a \in G\) . \(\varphi(e_G) = e_H\) . \(\varphi(a^{-1}) = \varphi(a)^{-1}\) . \(\ker \varphi\) is a subgroup of \(G\) . \(\varphi(a^n) = \varphi(a)^n\) for every \(n \in \nZ\) . The image \(\varphi(G)\) is a subgroup of \(H\) .

title: Definition 3.4.2 (Cycle, Transposition)
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) and \(k \ge 2\) , and let \(i_1, \dots, i_k \in \{1, \dots, n\}\) be distinct . The \(k\) -cycle \((i_1\ i_2\ \cdots\ i_k) \in S_n\) is the permutation \(\gamma\) with \[ \gamma(i_j) \coloneqq i_{j+1} \ \text{ for } 1 \le j < k , \qquad \gamma(i_k) \coloneqq i_1 , \] and \(\gamma(x) \coloneqq x\) for every \(x \in \{1, \dots, n\}\) not among \(i_1, \dots, i_k\) . A \(2\) -cycle \((i\ j)\) is a transposition . Two cycles are disjoint if their supports are disjoint.

title: Definition 3.4.1 (Permutations and the Symmetric Group)
content: Let \(X\) be a set. A permutation of \(X\) is a bijection \(X \to X\) . The permutations of \(X\) , with the operation \(\sigma\tau \coloneqq \sigma \circ \tau\) , form the group \(S_X\) of @exm-groups (c). For \(n \in \nN\) , the symmetric group is \[ S_n \coloneqq S_{\{1, \dots, n\}} , \] where \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) is empty for \(n = 0\) . The support of \(\sigma \in S_X\) is the set of points it moves, \[ \supp \sigma \coloneqq \{ x \in X : \sigma(x) \ne x \} . \]

title: Example (Computing with Cycles)
content: In \(S_3\) , compute \((1\ 3)(1\ 2)\) and \((1\ 2)(1\ 3)\) . In \(S_5\) , write \[ \sigma = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 3 & 5 & 1 & 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \] as a product of cycles.

Run the proof of @thm-disjoint-cycle-decomposition on \[ \sigma = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in S_5 , \] starting at \(i = 1\) : give the orbit of \(1\) , the number \(r\) , the cycle \(\gamma\) , and \(\rho = \gamma^{-1}\sigma\) ; then finish the run. Let \(\sigma\) be a \(k\) -cycle and \(\tau\) an \(l\) -cycle in \(S_n\) , disjoint. Prove that, for every \(m \in \nZ_{>0}\) , \((\sigma\tau)^m = \id\) if and only if \(k \mid m\) and \(l \mid m\) . title: Lemma 3.4.1 (Permutations Fixing the Last Point)
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) , and let \(S' \coloneqq \{ \sigma \in S_{n+1} : \sigma(n + 1) = n + 1 \}\) , a subgroup of \(S_{n+1}\) . For \(\sigma \in S'\) , the restriction \(\sigma'\) of \(\sigma\) to \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) , with codomain \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) , is a permutation of \(\{1, \dots, n\}\) . The map \(S' \to S_n\) , \(\sigma \mapsto \sigma'\) , is an isomorphism. Its inverse sends \(\rho \in S_n\) to its extension \(\bar\rho \in S'\) , defined by \(\bar\rho(i) \coloneqq \rho(i)\) for \(i \le n\) and \(\bar\rho(n + 1) \coloneqq n + 1\) .

title: Proposition 3.4.3 (Disjoint Permutations Commute)
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) and \(\sigma, \tau \in S_n\) with \(\supp \sigma \cap \supp \tau = \emptyset\) . Then \(\sigma\tau = \tau\sigma\) . Moreover, every permutation \(\sigma\) maps \(\supp \sigma\) onto itself: \(\sigma(\supp \sigma) = \supp \sigma\) .

title: Proposition 3.4.2 (The Symmetric Group Has n! Elements)
content: For every \(n \in \nN\) , \(S_n\) is finite and has \(n!\) elements: \(\card{S_n} = n!\) .

title: Theorem 3.4.4 (Disjoint Cycle Decomposition)
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) . Every \(\sigma \in S_n\) is a product \(\sigma = \gamma_1 \gamma_2 \cdots \gamma_s\) , \(s \in \nN\) , of pairwise disjoint cycles, each with support contained in \(\supp \sigma\) . For \(\sigma = \id\) the product is empty ( \(s = 0\) ).

title: Corollary 3.5.3 (Adjacent Transpositions Generate S_n)
content: Let \(n \ge 2\) . Every \(\sigma \in S_n\) is a product of adjacent transpositions \((i\ \ i{+}1)\) , \(1 \le i < n\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Find the error)

(2) The cycle sends \(i_1\) to \(i_2\) , then \(i_2\) to \(i_3\) , and so on, up to \(i_k\) , which it sends back to \(i_1\) . title: Definition 4.1.1 (Polynomial)
content:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. A polynomial over \(R\) (in the indeterminate \(x\) ) is a function \(p \colon 
N 	o R\) , written \(p = (p_0, p_1, p_2, \dots)\) , such that only finitely many \(p_k\) are non-zero: there exists \(N \in 
N\) with \(p_k = 0\) for every \(k > N\) . Such an \(N\) is called admissible for \(p\) . The element \(p_k\) is the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \(p\) . For \(a \in R\) and \(n \in 
N\) , the monomial \(a \, x^n\) is the polynomial with \(a\) in position \(n\) and \(0\) in every other position. We set \(x \coloneqq 1 \, x^1\) , and for \(a \in R\) the constant \(a\) is the monomial \(a \, x^0\) . The zero polynomial is \(0 \coloneqq (0, 0, 0, \dots)\) . The set of all polynomials over \(R\) is written \(R[x]\) .

title: Lemma 4.1.1 (Finite Sums, Powers and Multiples)
content:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. (Sums.) Let \(T\) be a set with a function \(+ \colon T 	imes T 	o T\) and an element \(0 \in T\) with \(0 + u = u\) for every \(u \in T\) . For a sequence \((u_i)_{i \in 
N}\) in \(T\) there is exactly one way to define \(\sum_{i=0}^{k} u_i \in T\) , for \(k \in 
N\) , such that \[ \sum_{i=0}^{0} u_i = u_0 , \qquad \sum_{i=0}^{k+1} u_i = \sum_{i=0}^{k} u_i + u_{k+1} , \] starting from the empty sum \(0\) . The sum \(\sum_{i=0}^{k} u_i\) depends only on \(u_0, \dots, u_k\) ; so a finite list \(u_0, \dots, u_k\) has a sum, computed from any extension of the list to a sequence. Likewise, a finite list \(s_1, \dots, s_r\) in \(R\) has a product \(\prod_{j=1}^{r} s_j\) , with \(\prod_{j=1}^{0} s_j = 1\) and \(\prod_{j=1}^{r+1} s_j =  igl( \prod_{j=1}^{r} s_j  igr) s_{r+1}\) . (Rules for sums in \(R\) .) For \(k \in

N\) : if \(u_i = 0\) for every \(i \le k\) with \(i 
e j\) , then \(\sum_{i=0}^{k} u_i = u_j\) when \(j \le k\) , and \(\sum_{i=0}^{k} u_i = 0\) when \(j > k\) ; (Σ4) \(-\sum_{i=0}^{k} u_i = \sum_{i=0}^{k} (-u_i)\) . (Powers.) For \(s \in R\) and \(n \in 
N\) , \(s^0 \coloneqq 1\) and \(s^{n+1} \coloneqq s^n s\) define \(s^n\) for every \(n\) , and for all \(s, t \in R\) and \(m, n \in 
N\) , \[ s^{m+n} = s^m s^n , \qquad (s^m)^n = s^{mn} , \qquad (st)^n = s^n t^n . \] (Multiples.) For all \(a, b \in R\) and \(m, n \in 
Z\) , \[  egin{aligned} (m + n) \cdot a &= m \cdot a + n \cdot a , & m \cdot (a + b) &= m \cdot a + m \cdot b , \ (m \cdot a) b &= m \cdot (ab) , & (m \cdot 1) a &= m \cdot a , \ (mn) \cdot a &= m \cdot (n \cdot a) . \end{aligned} \]

title: Definition 4.2.1 (The Polynomial Ring)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. For \(p, q \in R[x]\) and \(k \in \nN\) define \[ (p + q)_k \coloneqq p_k + q_k , \qquad (-p)_k \coloneqq -p_k , \qquad (pq)_k \coloneqq \sum_{i=0}^{k} p_i \, q_{k-i} . \] The set \(R[x]\) with this addition and this multiplication is the polynomial ring over \(R\) .

Then \(\sigma(p)\) is a polynomial, since \((-1)^k \cdot 0 = 0\) . We want to prove that \(\sigma(pq) = \sigma(p) \sigma(q)\) for all \(p, q \in R[x]\) . You may use the following, without proof. The map \(\sigma\) is additive: \(\sigma(p + q) = \sigma(p) + \sigma(q)\) , position by position by (F9). Hence, with ( \(\ast\) ) and ( \(\ast\ast\) ), the maps \(\Phi(p, q) \coloneqq \sigma(pq)\) and \(\Psi(p, q) \coloneqq \sigma(p) \sigma(q)\) are additive in each argument. The last step is blank. title: Exercise (C2: Formal power series)
Lemma 4.2.3 (Check on Monomials)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, and let \(T\) be a set with a function \(+ \colon T \times T \to T\) . Let \(\Phi, \Psi\) be maps of one, two or three polynomial arguments to \(T\) , that is, both maps \(R[x] \to T\) , both \(R[x]^2 \to T\) or both \(R[x]^3 \to T\) , that are additive in each argument : for each argument position and all fixed values of the other arguments, \[ \Phi(\dots, u + u', \dots) = \Phi(\dots, u, \dots) + \Phi(\dots, u', \dots) \] with \(u, u'\) in that position, and the same for \(\Psi\) . If \(\Phi\) and \(\Psi\) take the same value whenever every argument is a monomial, then \(\Phi = \Psi\) .

title: Lemma 4.2.2 (Multiplying by a Monomial)
content: Let \(a, b \in R\) , \(m, n \in \nN\) and \(q \in R[x]\) . \(\bigl( (a x^m) q \bigr)_k = a \, q_{k-m}\) for \(k \ge m\) , and \(\bigl( (a x^m) q \bigr)_k = 0\) for \(k < m\) . \((a x^m)(b x^n) = (ab) \, x^{m+n}\) .

title: Proposition 4.2.1 (A Polynomial Is the Sum of Its Monomials)
content: Let \(p \in R[x]\) and \(N \in \nN\) . The sum \(\sum_{k=0}^{N} p_k x^k\) of the monomials \(p_k x^k\) , formed in \((R[x], +)\) , has coefficient \(p_j\) in position \(j\) for every \(j \le N\) , and \(0\) in every position \(j > N\) . In particular, if \(N\) is admissible for \(p\) , then \[ p = \sum_{k=0}^{N} p_k x^k . \]

title: Theorem 4.2.4 (The Polynomial Ring Is a Commutative Ring)
content:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. \(R[x]\) , with the operations of @def-polynomial-ring , is a commutative ring ( @fd3:def-commutative-ring-and-field ), with zero the zero polynomial, negative \(-p\) as defined there, and one \(1 \coloneqq 1 \, x^0\) . Spelled out, for all \(p, q, r \in R[x]\) : (1) \(p + q = q + p\) and \((p + q) + r = p + (q + r)\) ; (2) \(p + 0 = p\) and \(p + (-p) = 0\) ; (3) \(pq = qp\) and \((pq)r = p(qr)\) ; (4) \(1 \cdot p = p\) ; (5) \(p(q + r) = pq + pr\) . The map \(R 	o R[x]\) , \(a \mapsto a \, x^0\) , is injective and satisfies \((a + b) x^0 = a x^0 + b x^0\) , \((ab) x^0 = (a x^0)(b x^0)\) and \(1 x^0 = 1\) . If \(1 
e 0\) in \(R\) , then \(1 
e 0\) in \(R[x]\) . For \(n \in 
N\) , the \(n\) -th power of \(x\) in the ring \(R[x]\) ( @lem-finite-sums-and-powers (c)) is the monomial \(1 \, x^n\) , and the product of the constant \(a\) with it is the monomial \(a \, x^n\) . Hence \(p = \sum_{k=0}^{N} p_k x^k\) , for admissible \(N\) , is a sum of products of constants and powers of \(x\) . For a constant \(a\) and \(p \in R[x]\) , \((ap)_k = a \, p_k\) for every \(k\) .

title: Corollary 4.3.3 (Polynomial Rings over Integral Domains)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. If \(R\) is an integral domain, \(p, q \in R[x]\) and \(pq = 0\) , then \(p = 0\) or \(q = 0\) . So \(R[x]\) is an integral domain. (Cancellation) If \(R\) is an integral domain, \(p, q, r \in R[x]\) , \(pq = pr\) and \(p \ne 0\) , then \(q = r\) . Conversely, if \(R[x]\) is an integral domain, then so is \(R\) .

title: Definition 4.3.2 (Integral Domain)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: An integral domain is a commutative ring \(R\) with \(1 \ne 0\) and no zero divisors : for all \(a, b \in R\) , if \(ab = 0\) , then \(a = 0\) or \(b = 0\) .

title: Definition 4.3.3 (Polynomials of Degree at Most n)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(n \in \nN\) . The set of polynomials of degree at most \(n\) is \[ R[x]_{\le n} \coloneqq \{ p \in R[x] : \deg p \le n \} . \]

title: Definition 4.3.4 (Polynomials of Degree Exactly n)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(n \in \nN\) . The set of polynomials of degree exactly \(n\) is \(R[x]_{= n} \coloneqq \{ p \in R[x] : \deg p = n \}\) .

title: Proposition 4.3.4 (Units of a Polynomial Ring)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: Let \(R\) be an integral domain. Then the units of \(R[x]\) are exactly the constants \(a\) with \(a \in R^{\times}\) ( @def-ring-unit ): identifying \(a\) with \(a x^0\) , \((R[x])^{\times} = R^{\times}\) .

title: Theorem 4.3.2 (Degree of a Product)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, let \(p, q \in R[x]\) be non-zero, and let \(m \coloneqq \deg p\) , \(n \coloneqq \deg q\) . \((pq)_k = 0\) for every \(k > m + n\) , and \((pq)_{m+n} = \operatorname{lc}(p) \operatorname{lc}(q)\) . Hence \(\deg(pq) \le \deg p + \deg q\) for all \(p, q \in R[x]\) , zero or not; and if \(p = 0\) or \(q = 0\) , then \(pq = 0\) and \(\deg(pq) = -\infty = \deg p + \deg q\) . \(\deg(pq) = m + n\) if and only if \(\operatorname{lc}(p) \operatorname{lc}(q) \ne 0\) , and then \(\operatorname{lc}(pq) = \operatorname{lc}(p) \operatorname{lc}(q)\) . This holds in particular when \(R\) has no zero divisors ( \(ab = 0\) implies \(a = 0\) or \(b = 0\) ), for example when \(R\) is a field ( @thm-field-basic-properties (f)); together with the last clause of (a), \(\deg(pq) = \deg p + \deg q\) then holds for all \(p, q \in R[x]\) , zero or not; when \(\operatorname{lc}(p)\) is a unit of \(R\) ( @def-ring-unit ), in particular when \(p\) is monic.

title: Theorem 4.3.1 (Degree of a Sum)
page: 4.3 Degree, Leading Coefficients, and Integral Domains
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(p, q \in R[x]\) . Then \[ \deg(p + q) \le \max(\deg p, \deg q) , \] with equality when \(\deg p \ne \deg q\) .

title: Corollary 4.4.3 (Changing the Coefficient Ring)
content: Let \(\varphi \colon R \to S\) be a ring homomorphism. For \(p \in R[x]\) , let \(\varphi_*(p)\) be the sequence with \(\bigl(\varphi_*(p)\bigr)_k \coloneqq \varphi(p_k)\) . Then \(\varphi_*(p) \in S[x]\) , and \(\varphi_* \colon R[x] \to S[x]\) is a ring homomorphism with \(\varphi_*(a x^n) = \varphi(a) x^n\) . Moreover \(\deg \varphi_*(p) \le \deg p\) for every \(p\) , and for \(p \ne 0\) , equality holds if and only if \(\varphi(\operatorname{lc}(p)) \ne 0\) .

title: Definition 4.4.3 (Composition of Polynomials)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(p, q \in R[x]\) . The composition \(p \circ q \in R[x]\) is \(\Phi(p)\) for the homomorphism \(\Phi\) of @thm-polynomial-substitution with \(S = R[x]\) , \(\varphi \colon a \mapsto a x^0\) and \(s = q\) : \[ p \circ q = \sum_{k=0}^{N} p_k \, q^k \qquad (N \text{ admissible for } p). \]

title: Definition 4.4.1 (Evaluation, Root, Polynomial Function)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, \(p \in R[x]\) and \(c \in R\) . The value of \(p\) at \(c\) is \[ p(c) \coloneqq \sum_{k=0}^{N} p_k c^k \in R , \] for any \(N \in \nN\) with \(p_k = 0\) for every \(k > N\) . The element \(c\) is a root of \(p\) if \(p(c) = 0\) . The polynomial function of \(p\) is the function \(R \to R\) , \(c \mapsto p(c)\) .

title: Definition 4.4.2 (Ring Homomorphism)
content: Let \(R\) and \(S\) be commutative rings. A ring homomorphism \(\varphi \colon R \to S\) is a function such that, for all \(a, b \in R\) , \[ \varphi(a + b) = \varphi(a) + \varphi(b) , \qquad \varphi(ab) = \varphi(a) \varphi(b) , \] and \(\varphi(1) = 1\) .

title: Proposition 4.4.4 (Polynomials and Their Functions)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring. The set \(R^R\) of functions \(R \to R\) ( @fd2:def-function ), with the pointwise operations \((f + g)(c) \coloneqq f(c) + g(c)\) and \((fg)(c) \coloneqq f(c) g(c)\) , is a commutative ring, whose zero and one are the constant functions with values \(0\) and \(1\) . The map \(\varepsilon \colon R[x] \to R^R\) , \(\varepsilon(p) \coloneqq (c \mapsto p(c))\) , is a ring homomorphism. For all \(p, q \in R[x]\) and \(c \in R\) , \((p \circ q)(c) = p(q(c))\) : composition of polynomials matches composition of their functions. If \(R\) is finite with \(1 \ne 0\) , then \(\varepsilon\) is not injective. Explicitly, if \(c_1, \dots, c_r\) lists the elements of \(R\) without repetition, then \[ P \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^{r} (x - c_j) \] is monic of degree \(r\) , so \(P \ne 0\) , yet \(P(c) = 0\) for every \(c \in R\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.1 (Evaluation Respects the Operations)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, \(p, q \in R[x]\) and \(c \in R\) . Then \[ (p + q)(c) = p(c) + q(c) , \qquad (pq)(c) = p(c) \, q(c) , \] and \(a(c) = a\) for every constant \(a\) , and \(x(c) = c\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.2 (Substitution Principle)
content: Let \(R\) and \(S\) be commutative rings, \(\varphi \colon R \to S\) a ring homomorphism, and \(s \in S\) . Define \(\Phi \colon R[x] \to S\) by \[ \Phi(p) \coloneqq \sum_{k=0}^{N} \varphi(p_k) \, s^k , \] for any \(N\) admissible for \(p\) . \(\Phi\) is well defined, and it is a ring homomorphism with \(\Phi(a) = \varphi(a)\) for every constant \(a \in R\) and \(\Phi(x) = s\) . \(\Phi\) is the only ring homomorphism \(R[x] \to S\) with these two properties.

title: Proposition 4.5.2 (When the Formal Derivative Is Zero)
content: Let \(F\) be a field ( @def-field ) and \(f \in F[x]\) . If \(\operatorname{char} F = 0\) , then \(f' = 0\) if and only if \(f\) is constant. Moreover, \(\deg f' = \deg f - 1\) whenever \(\deg f \ge 1\) . If \(\operatorname{char} F = p > 0\) , then \(p\) is prime, and the following are equivalent: (i) \(f' = 0\) ; (ii) \(f_k = 0\) for every \(k \in \nN\) not divisible by \(p\) ; (iii) \(f = g \circ x^p\) for some \(g \in F[x]\) ( @def-polynomial-composition ).

title: Theorem 4.5.1 (Rules for the Formal Derivative)
content: Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, \(f, g \in R[x]\) , \(a, c \in R\) and \(m \in \nZ_{>0}\) . (Linearity) \((f + g)' = f' + g'\) , and \((af)' = a f'\) for the constant \(a\) ; moreover \(a' = 0\) . (Product rule) \((fg)' = f'g + fg'\) . (Power rule) \((g^m)' = (m \cdot 1) \, g^{m-1} g'\) . In particular \(\bigl( (x - c)^m \bigr)' = (m \cdot 1)(x - c)^{m-1}\) .

title: Definition 5.1.1 (Divisibility of Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . \(g\) divides \(f\) over \(F\) , written \(g \mid f\) , if there exists \(h \in F[x]\) with \(f = gh\) . Then \(g\) is a divisor (or factor ) of \(f\) , and \(f\) is a multiple of \(g\) . We write \(g \nmid f\) when \(g\) does not divide \(f\) . \(f\) and \(g\) are associates if \(f = cg\) for some non-zero constant \(c \in F\) .

title: Example (Remainders without dividing)
content: In \(\nQ[x]\) , find the remainder of \(f = x^5 - 3x^3 + 2x + 7\) on division by \(x - 2\) . In \(\nQ[x]\) , find the remainder of \(x^5\) on division by \(x^2 - x\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State @thm-polynomial-division-remainder with every hypothesis. Name the two places in its proof where “ \(F\) is a field” is used. Let \(f \in F[x]\) , and let \(c \in F\) be a non-zero constant. What are the quotient and the remainder of \(f\) on division by \(c\) ? True or false, with a reason: for \(f, g \in \nQ[x]\) , if \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid f\) , then \(f = g\) . The same question in \(\nF_2[x]\) .

title: Exercise (B1: Two long divisions)
content:
In \(
Q[x]\) , divide \(x^4 - 3x^3 + 2x - 5\) by \(3x^2 - 1\) . In \(
F_5[x]\) , divide \(x^4 + 2x^3 + 3x + 1\) by \(2x^2 + 3\) , and decide whether \(2x^2 + 3\) divides \(x^4 + 2x^3 + 3x + 1\) in \(
F_5[x]\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A factor of a difference of powers)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(c \in F\) and \(n \in \nZ_{>0}\) . Deduce from @fd4:lem-difference-of-powers that \[ x^n - c^n = (x - c) \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} c^j x^{n-1-j} , \] and hence that \(x - c \mid x^n - c^n\) . Then give a second proof of the divisibility with @thm-polynomial-remainder-factor .

title: Exercise (B3: One remainder over every field)
content: Let \(F\) be any field. Show that the remainder of \(x^{100}\) on division by \(x^2 - 1\) in \(F[x]\) is \(1\) . Then explain why, over \(\nQ\) , evaluating at the roots \(1\) and \(-1\) also finds it, and why that method alone does not settle the question over \(\nF_2\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Monic divisors keep integer coefficients)
content:
Call \(p \in 
Q[x]\) an integer polynomial if every coefficient of \(p\) lies in \(
Z\) . Let \(f, g\) be integer polynomials with \(g\) monic. Prove that the quotient and the remainder of \(f\) on division by \(g\) in \(
Q[x]\) are integer polynomials. Prove the same if \(\operatorname{lc}(g) = -1\) . Explain why the least-degree argument of @thm-polynomial-division-remainder still works when \(S\) is replaced by \(\{ f - hg : h 	ext{ an integer polynomial} \}\) , for \(g\) monic.

title: Exercise (C2: The remainder modulo a quadratic with known roots)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) and \(a, b \in F\) . If \(a \ne b\) , prove that the remainder of \(f\) on division by \((x - a)(x - b)\) is \[ f(a) (a - b)^{-1} (x - b) + f(b) (b - a)^{-1} (x - a) . \] If \(a = b\) , write \(f = (x - a)h + f(a)\) ( @thm-polynomial-remainder-factor (a)) and prove that the remainder of \(f\) on division by \((x - a)^2\) is \(h(a)(x - a) + f(a)\) . Hence find the remainder of \(x^{100}\) on division by \(x^2 - 3x + 2\) in \(\nQ[x]\) .

title: Proposition 5.1.1 (Rules for Divisibility of Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, h \in F[x]\) . \(g \mid 0\) . \(0 \mid f\) if and only if \(f = 0\) . Every non-zero constant divides every polynomial. If \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid h\) , then \(f \mid h\) . If \(h \mid f\) and \(h \mid g\) , then \(h \mid af + bg\) for all \(a, b \in F[x]\) . If \(g \mid f\) and \(f \ne 0\) , then \(\deg g \le \deg f\) . The units of \(F[x]\) ( @def-ring-unit ) are exactly the non-zero constants. \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid f\) if and only if \(f\) and \(g\) are associates (this includes \(f = g = 0\) ). Every non-zero \(f\) has exactly one monic associate, namely \(\operatorname{lc}(f)^{-1} f\) . Two monic polynomials that divide each other are equal.

title: Theorem 5.1.2 (Division with Remainder in F[x])
content: Let \(F\) be a field, and let \(f, g \in F[x]\) with \(g \ne 0\) . There are unique \(q, r \in F[x]\) with \[ f = qg + r \quad \text{and} \quad \deg r < \deg g . \] \(g \mid f\) if and only if \(r = 0\) . The polynomials \(q\) and \(r\) are the quotient and the remainder of \(f\) on division by \(g\) .

title: Theorem 5.1.3 (Remainder Theorem and Factor Theorem)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) and \(c \in F\) . The remainder of \(f\) on division by \(x - c\) is the constant \(f(c)\) . \(c\) is a root of \(f\) if and only if \(x - c \mid f\) . \(f\) has a factor of degree \(1\) in \(F[x]\) if and only if \(f\) has a root in \(F\) .

title: Corollary 5.2.3 (Coprime Means 1 Is a Combination)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . Then \(f\) and \(g\) are coprime if and only if \(af + bg = 1\) for some \(a, b \in F[x]\) .

title: Definition 5.2.3 (Coprime Polynomials)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field. Polynomials \(f, g \in F[x]\) are coprime over \(F\) if \(\gcd(f, g) = 1\) .

title: Definition 5.2.1 (Ideal Generated by Polynomials)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(k \in \nZ_{>0}\) and \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in F[x]\) . The set \[ \langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle \coloneqq \{ a_1 f_1 + \dots + a_k f_k : a_1, \dots, a_k \in F[x] \} \] is the ideal generated by \(f_1, \dots, f_k\) . For one polynomial, \(\langle f \rangle = \{ af : a \in F[x] \}\) is the set of multiples of \(f\) .

title: Definition 5.2.2 (Greatest Common Divisor of Polynomials)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) , not both \(0\) . A greatest common divisor of \(f\) and \(g\) is a monic \(d \in F[x]\) such that \(d \mid f\) , \(d \mid g\) , and \(h \mid d\) for every common divisor \(h\) of \(f\) and \(g\) . We set \(\gcd(0, 0) \coloneqq 0\) .

title: Example (A run of the Euclidean algorithm)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: In \(\nQ[x]\) , compute \(\gcd(f, g)\) for \(f = x^4 - x^3 - 3x^2 + x + 2\) and \(g = x^3 - 2x - 1\) , and write it as \(af + bg\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: These questions are about the proof of @thm-polynomial-ideals-principal . Where is “least degree” used? Why is \(d\) made monic, and what would fail without it? Run the proof on \(I \coloneqq \{ f \in \nQ[x] : f(1) = 0 \text{ and } f(-1) = 0 \}\) : show that \(I\) is an ideal, and find \(d\) . The polynomials in two indeterminates \(x, y\) over \(\nQ\) with zero constant term (such as \(x\) , \(y\) , \(x^2 y - 3y\) ) are closed under sums and under multiplication by any polynomial in \(x, y\) . Name the step of the proof that has no analogue there. (A prose answer; no proof that the theorem fails is asked for.) State the idea of the proof in two sentences.

title: Exercise (B1: A gcd and its common root)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: In \(\nQ[x]\) , let \(f = x^3 + x^2 + x + 1\) and \(g = x^3 + x + 2\) . Compute \(\gcd(f, g)\) with the Euclidean algorithm, and write it as \(af + bg\) . Hence show that \(-1\) is the only common root of \(f\) and \(g\) in \(\nQ\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A gcd over the field with two elements)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: In \(\nF_2[x]\) , let \(f = x^4 + x^3 + x + 1\) and \(g = x^3 + x^2 + x + 1\) . Show that \(\gcd(f, g) = x^2 + 1\) and that \(x^2 + 1 = 1 \cdot f + x \cdot g\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Exit check: ideals of F[x] and Bézout)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field. Prove that for every ideal \(I \ne \{0\}\) of \(F[x]\) there is exactly one monic \(d\) with \(I = \langle d \rangle\) . Let \(f, g \in F[x]\) , not both \(0\) , and let \(d\) be the monic generator of \(\langle f, g \rangle\) . Prove that \(d \mid f\) , \(d \mid g\) , that every common divisor of \(f\) and \(g\) divides \(d\) , that \(d = \gcd(f, g)\) , and that \(d = af + bg\) for some \(a, b \in F[x]\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Scaling the gcd)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f, g \in F[x]\) , and \(h \in F[x]\) monic. Prove that \(\gcd(hf, hg) = h \gcd(f, g)\) .

title: Exercise (C3: The gcd of two binomials)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field. For \(m, n \in \nN\) , not both \(0\) , prove that \[ \gcd(x^m - 1, \, x^n - 1) = x^{\gcd(m, n)} - 1 \] in \(F[x]\) (here \(x^0 - 1 = 0\) , and \(\gcd(m, n)\) is the integer gcd). Compute \(\gcd(x^{12} - 1, x^{18} - 1)\) .

title: Lemma 5.2.4 (One Step of the Euclidean Algorithm)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, q, r \in F[x]\) with \(f = qg + r\) . Then \(\langle f, g \rangle = \langle g, r \rangle\) , and hence \(\gcd(f, g) = \gcd(g, r)\) .

title: Proposition 5.2.6 (Division and gcd Do Not Depend on the Field)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(L\) be a field, \(K \subseteq L\) a subfield, and \(f, g \in K[x]\) . If \(g \ne 0\) , the quotient and the remainder of \(f\) on division by \(g\) are the same in \(K[x]\) and in \(L[x]\) . If \(g \ne 0\) , then \(g \mid f\) in \(L[x]\) if and only if \(g \mid f\) in \(K[x]\) . \(\gcd(f, g)\) is the same computed in \(K[x]\) or in \(L[x]\) . In particular, \(f\) and \(g\) are coprime over \(K\) if and only if they are coprime over \(L\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.5 (The Euclidean Algorithm for Polynomials)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm

title: Theorem 5.2.2 (Bézout’s Theorem for Polynomials)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field, let \(f, g \in F[x]\) be not both \(0\) , and let \(d\) be the monic polynomial with \(\langle f, g \rangle = \langle d \rangle\) ( @thm-polynomial-ideals-principal ). \(d \mid f\) and \(d \mid g\) . Every common divisor of \(f\) and \(g\) divides \(d\) . \(d = \gcd(f, g)\) . So \(\gcd(f, g)\) exists, and \(\langle f, g \rangle = \langle \gcd(f, g) \rangle\) . \(\gcd(f, g) = af + bg\) for some \(a, b \in F[x]\) . \(\gcd(f, g)\) has the largest degree among the common divisors of \(f\) and \(g\) , and a common divisor of that degree is an associate of \(\gcd(f, g)\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.1 (Ideals of F[x] Are Principal)
page: 5.2 Ideals, the Greatest Common Divisor, and the Euclidean Algorithm
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(I\) an ideal of \(F[x]\) . If \(I = \{0\}\) , then \(I = \langle 0 \rangle\) . If \(I \ne \{0\}\) , there is exactly one monic \(d \in F[x]\) with \(I = \langle d \rangle\) . Moreover \(d\) is the only monic element of \(I\) of least degree among the non-zero elements of \(I\) .

title: Corollary 5.3.3 (An Irreducible Dividing a Product)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) . For every \(f \in F[x]\) : \(p \mid f\) or \(\gcd(p, f) = 1\) . For all \(g, h \in F[x]\) : if \(p \mid gh\) , then \(p \mid g\) or \(p \mid h\) . If \((q_1, \dots, q_l)\) is a list of polynomials in \(F[x]\) , with \(l \in \nN\) , and \(p \mid q_1 q_2 \cdots q_l\) , then \(l \ge 1\) and \(p \mid q_j\) for some \(j \in \{1, \dots, l\}\) . If \(p\) and \(q\) are monic and irreducible over \(F\) and \(p \mid q\) , then \(p = q\) .

title: Definition 5.3.1 (Irreducible Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) . The polynomial \(p\) is irreducible over \(F\) if \(\deg p \ge 1\) and, whenever \(p = gh\) with \(g, h \in F[x]\) , one of \(g\) , \(h\) is a constant. A polynomial of degree at least \(1\) that is not irreducible over \(F\) is reducible over \(F\) .

title: Example (A Cubic with No Rational Root)
content: Show that \(3x^3 + x^2 - 2\) is irreducible over \(\nQ\) .

content:
Factor \(x^4 - 1\) into monic irreducibles over \(
Q\) , over \(
R\) , over \(

title: Exercise (A1)
content: These questions are about the uniqueness half of the proof of @thm-polynomial-unique-factorization . Which line of the proof uses Euclid’s lemma, and through which result? Where is “monic” used? In \(\nF_5[x]\) , run the induction step on the two lists \((p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4) = (x - 1, x - 2, x - 3, x - 4)\) and \((q_1, q_2, q_3, q_4) = (x - 4, x - 3, x - 2, x - 1)\) . Which \(j\) matches \(p_4\) ? What is the bijection \(\sigma\) at the end? Why must the empty list be allowed? Give the idea of the uniqueness proof in two sentences.

title: Exercise (B3: The small irreducibles over the two-element field)
content: List all irreducible polynomials of degree at most \(3\) over \(\nF_2\) , and prove that the list is complete.

title: Exercise (C1: Exit check: unique factorization)
content: Prove the uniqueness half of @thm-polynomial-unique-factorization : if \(c \, p_1 \cdots p_k = c' q_1 \cdots q_l\) with \(c, c' \in F\) non-zero and all \(p_i\) , \(q_j\) monic irreducible over the field \(F\) , then \(c = c'\) , \(l = k\) , and the two lists agree up to a bijection of indices. You may cite Euclid’s lemma ( @thm-polynomial-euclid-lemma ) and @cor-irreducible-divides-product .

title: Exercise (C2: Find the error)
content:
Here is a statement and an argument for it. Claim. \(x^4 + 1\) is irreducible over \(
Q\) . Argument. (1) By @thm-rational-root-test , a rational root of \(x^4 + 1\) is \(u/v\) with \(u \mid 1\) and \(v \mid 1\) , so the only candidates are \(1\) and \(-1\) . (2) Both give the value \(1 + 1 = 2 
e 0\) , so \(x^4 + 1\) has no rational root. (3) By @prp-irreducible-low-degree , a polynomial without roots is irreducible. (4) Hence \(x^4 + 1\) is irreducible over \(
Q\) . Is the claim true? Does the argument prove it? If not, name the line that fails, explain why, give a counterexample to the step, and repair the proof.

title: Exercise (C3: Infinitely many irreducibles)
content:
Let \(F\) be a field. Prove that no finite list contains every monic irreducible polynomial of \(F[x]\) : for every list \((p_1, \dots, p_k)\) of monic irreducibles, \(k \in 
N\) , some monic irreducible is not an entry of it. Let \(p\) be prime. Prove that there are exactly \(p^n\) monic polynomials of degree \(n\) in \(
F_p[x]\) , for each \(n \in 
N\) , and deduce that \(
F_p[x]\) has monic irreducibles of arbitrarily large degree.

title: Exercise (C4: Greatest common divisor and least common multiple)
content: Let \(f, g \in F[x]\) be monic, \(d \coloneqq \gcd(f, g)\) , and write \(f = d f_1\) , \(g = d g_1\) . Prove that \(\gcd(f_1, g_1) = 1\) . Prove that \(L \coloneqq d f_1 g_1\) is a monic common multiple of \(f\) and \(g\) that divides every common multiple of \(f\) and \(g\) , and that \(d \cdot L = fg\) . In \(\nQ[x]\) , let \(f = g = 2x\) (not monic). The gcd is \(x\) , and the monic common multiple dividing every common multiple is \(x\) . Show that \(\gcd(f, g) \cdot x \ne fg\) .

title: Lemma 5.3.5 (An Irreducible Factor Exists)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) with \(\deg f \ge 1\) . Then \(f\) has a monic irreducible divisor in \(F[x]\) .

title: Proposition 5.3.1 (Irreducibility in Low Degree)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) . If \(\deg p \ge 2\) and \(p\) has a root in \(F\) , then \(p\) is reducible over \(F\) . If \(\deg p \in \{2, 3\}\) , then \(p\) is irreducible over \(F\) if and only if \(p\) has no root in \(F\) .

title: Proposition 5.3.4 (Coprime Divisors of a Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(m, n, h \in F[x]\) with \(m \mid h\) , \(n \mid h\) and \(\gcd(m, n) = 1\) . Then \(mn \mid h\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.2 (Euclid’s Lemma for Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, h \in F[x]\) . If \(f \mid gh\) and \(\gcd(f, g) = 1\) , then \(f \mid h\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.6 (Unique Factorization of Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) with \(\deg f \ge 1\) and leading coefficient \(c\) . Existence. There are \(k \ge 1\) and monic polynomials \(p_1, \dots, p_k\) , irreducible over \(F\) , with \(f = c \, p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k\) . Uniqueness. If also \(f = c' q_1 q_2 \cdots q_l\) with \(c' \in F\) , \(l \in \nN\) and monic polynomials \(q_1, \dots, q_l\) irreducible over \(F\) , then \(c' = c\) , \(l = k\) , and there is a bijection \(\sigma \colon \{1, \dots, k\} \to \{1, \dots, l\}\) ( @fd2:def-bijective ) with \(q_{\sigma(i)} = p_i\) for every \(i\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.7 (Rational Root Test)
content:
Let \(n \ge 1\) , let \(a_0, a_1, \dots, a_n \in 
Z\) with \(a_n 
e 0\) , and let \(f \coloneqq \sum_{i=0}^{n} a_i x^i \in 
Q[x]\) . If \(u \in 
Z\) , \(v \in 
Z_{>0}\) , \(\gcd(u, v) = 1\) and \(f(u/v) = 0\) , then \(u \mid a_0\) and \(v \mid a_n\) in \(
Z\) .

title: Corollary 5.4.8 (Repeated Factors and the Greatest Common Divisor)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) with \(\deg f \ge 1\) . If \(p \in F[x]\) is irreducible and \(p^2 \mid f\) , then \(p \mid \gcd(f, f')\) . So if \(\gcd(f, f') = 1\) , no irreducible divides \(f\) twice, and \(f\) has no multiple root in \(F\) . If \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) ( @def-characteristic ) and \(\gcd(f, f') \ne 1\) , then \(p^2 \mid f\) for some irreducible \(p\) .

title: Definition 5.4.1 (Multiplicity of a Root)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero , and \(c \in F\) . The multiplicity of \(c\) in \(f\) , written \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f)\) , is the largest \(m \in \nN\) with \((x - c)^m \mid f\) . The root \(c\) is simple if \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = 1\) and multiple if \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) \ge 2\) .

title: Definition 5.4.2 (Splitting over a Field)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero of degree \(n\) . The polynomial \(f\) splits over \(F\) if \[ f = a (x - a_1)(x - a_2) \cdots (x - a_n) \] for some \(a, a_1, \dots, a_n \in F\) , repetitions among the \(a_i\) allowed. For \(n = 0\) this says that \(f = a\) is a non-zero constant.

title: Exercise (B1: Put the proof in order)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: The following lines contain a proof of the divisibility part of @thm-polynomial-root-count , shuffled, together with two lines that do not belong. Write the seven correct lines in an order that makes a proof, say which other orders are also admissible, and say why each of the other two lines fails. We use induction on \(k\) ; for \(k = 1\) , \(x - c_1 \mid f\) by the factor theorem. Assume the claim for every list of \(k - 1\) distinct roots, and let \(c_1, \dots, c_k\) be distinct roots of \(f\) . Write \(f = (x - c_1) \cdots (x - c_{k-1}) \, h\) . Evaluate at \(c_k\) : \(0 = (c_k - c_1) \cdots (c_k - c_{k-1}) \, h(c_k)\) . Each \(c_k - c_i\) , \(i < k\) , is non-zero, since the roots are distinct. (v′) Each \(c_k - c_i\) , \(i < k\) , is non-zero, since \(c_k \ne 0\) . A product of non-zero elements of a field is non-zero, so \(h(c_k) = 0\) . (vi′) \(h(c_k) = 0\) , because \(f(c_k) = 0\) . By the factor theorem, \(h = (x - c_k) h_1\) , so \(f = (x - c_1) \cdots (x - c_k) \, h_1\) .

page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content:
Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero, \(c \in F\) and \(m \in 
N\) . \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = m\) if and only if \(f = (x - c)^m g\) for some \(g \in F[x]\) with \(g(c) 
e 0\) . Such a \(g\) is unique. If \(f = \sum_{j=0}^{n} b_j (x - c)^j\) is the expansion of @thm-polynomial-taylor-shift , then \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f)\) is the least \(j\) with \(b_j 
e 0\) .

title: Proposition 5.4.5 (Multiplicity of a Product)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f, g \in F[x]\) non-zero and \(c \in F\) . Then \(\operatorname{mult}_c(fg) = \operatorname{mult}_c(f) + \operatorname{mult}_c(g)\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.2 (Polynomials Determined by Values)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . Let \(n \in \nN\) . If \(\deg f \le n\) , \(\deg g \le n\) , and \(f(c_i) = g(c_i)\) for \(n + 1\) distinct elements \(c_0, \dots, c_n \in F\) , then \(f = g\) . If \(F\) is infinite and \(f(c) = g(c)\) for every \(c \in F\) , then \(f = g\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.7 (Repeated Roots and the Derivative)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero and \(c \in F\) . \(c\) is a multiple root of \(f\) if and only if \(f(c) = 0\) and \(f'(c) = 0\) . If \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = m \ge 1\) and \(m \cdot 1 \ne 0\) in \(F\) , then \(f' \ne 0\) and \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f') = m - 1\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.1 (Counting Roots)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) , \(k \ge 1\) , and let \(c_1, \dots, c_k \in F\) be distinct roots of \(f\) . Then \[ (x - c_1)(x - c_2) \cdots (x - c_k) \mid f . \] If \(f \ne 0\) , then \(k \le \deg f\) . In particular, a non-zero polynomial of degree \(n\) has at most \(n\) distinct roots in \(F\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.6 (Splitting Off All Roots)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) non-zero. Let \(c_1, \dots, c_k \in F\) , \(k \in \nN\) , be the distinct roots of \(f\) in \(F\) (every root of \(f\) in \(F\) is one of them), and \(m_i \coloneqq \operatorname{mult}_{c_i}(f)\) . Then \[ f = (x - c_1)^{m_1} (x - c_2)^{m_2} \cdots (x - c_k)^{m_k} \, g \] for some \(g \in F[x]\) with no root in \(F\) , and \(m_1 + m_2 + \dots + m_k \le \deg f\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.3 (Expansion in Powers of x - c)
page: 5.4 Roots, Multiplicity, and the Formal Derivative
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) with \(\deg f = n \ge 0\) , and \(c \in F\) . There are unique \(b_0, b_1, \dots, b_n \in F\) with \[ f = \sum_{j=0}^{n} b_j (x - c)^j . \] \(b_0 = f(c)\) , and \(b_n\) is the leading coefficient of \(f\) . For every \(h \in F\) , \(f(c + h) = \sum_{j=0}^{n} b_j h^j\) .

title: Definition 5.5.1 (Lagrange Polynomials)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content:
Let \(n \in

e i}}^{n} (c_i - c_j)^{-1} (x - c_j) \in F[x] , \] the product, in increasing order of \(j\) , of the \(n\) polynomials \((c_i - c_j)^{-1}(x - c_j)\) with \(j

title: Definition 5.5.2 (Congruence Modulo a Polynomial)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(m \in F[x]\) . Polynomials \(f, g \in F[x]\) are congruent modulo \(m\) , written \(f \equiv g \pmod{m}\) , if \(m \mid f - g\) ( @def-polynomial-divides ), that is, if \(f - g \in \langle m \rangle\) ( @def-polynomial-combinations ).

title: Lemma 5.5.4 (Coprime to Each Factor, Coprime to the Product)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(s \ge 1\) and \(p, q_1, \dots, q_s \in F[x]\) . If \(\gcd(p, q_j) = 1\) for every \(j\) , then \(\gcd(p, q_1 \cdots q_s) = 1\) . Let \(k \ge 1\) and let \(m_1, \dots, m_k \in F[x]\) be pairwise coprime : \(\gcd(m_i, m_j) = 1\) whenever \(i \ne j\) . If \(m_i \mid h\) for every \(i\) , then \(m_1 \cdots m_k \mid h\) .

title: Proposition 5.5.6 (Interpolation Is the Chinese Remainder Theorem for Linear Moduli)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) , let \(c_0, \dots, c_n \in F\) be distinct, let \(y_0, \dots, y_n \in F\) , and let \(m \coloneqq (x - c_0) \cdots (x - c_n)\) . The moduli \(x - c_0, \dots, x - c_n\) are pairwise coprime, and \(\deg m = n + 1\) . For \(f \in F[x]\) and each \(i\) : \(f \equiv y_i \pmod{x - c_i}\) if and only if \(f(c_i) = y_i\) . The polynomial of degree less than \(n + 1\) given by @thm-polynomial-chinese-remainder (c) for the right-hand sides \(y_0, \dots, y_n\) is \(\sum_{i} y_i \ell_i\) , the interpolating polynomial of @thm-polynomial-interpolation . In particular, the remainder of the polynomial \(e_i\) of @thm-polynomial-chinese-remainder (a) on division by \(m\) is the Lagrange polynomial \(\ell_i\) .

title: Theorem 5.5.5 (Chinese Remainder Theorem for Polynomials)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(k \ge 1\) , let \(m_1, \dots, m_k \in F[x]\) be non-zero and pairwise coprime, and let \(m \coloneqq m_1 \cdots m_k\) . For each \(i\) , let \(M_i\) be the product of the \(m_j\) with \(j \ne i\) (in increasing order of \(j\) ). For each \(i\) there are \(a_i, b_i \in F[x]\) with \(a_i M_i + b_i m_i = 1\) . Put \(e_i \coloneqq a_i M_i\) . Then \(e_i \equiv 1 \pmod{m_i}\) and \(e_i \equiv 0 \pmod{m_j}\) for \(j \ne i\) , and for all \(r_1, \dots, r_k \in F[x]\) the polynomial \(f \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^{k} r_i e_i\) satisfies \[ f \equiv r_i \pmod{m_i} \qquad \text{for every } i \in \{1, \dots, k\} . \] A polynomial \(g\) satisfies the same \(k\) congruences if and only if \(g \equiv f \pmod{m}\) . Exactly one polynomial of degree less than \(\deg m\) satisfies the \(k\) congruences. The rule \(\Phi([f]_m) \coloneqq ([f]_{m_1}, \dots, [f]_{m_k})\) is a well-defined bijection \[ \Phi \colon F[x]/\langle m \rangle \to F[x]/\langle m_1 \rangle \times \dots \times F[x]/\langle m_k \rangle , \] and, with \(+\) and \(\cdot\) on the right taken componentwise, \(\Phi\) preserves \(+\) and \(\cdot\) and sends \([1]_m\) to \(([1]_{m_1}, \dots, [1]_{m_k})\) .

title: Theorem 5.5.1 (Lagrange Interpolation)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(n \in \nN\) , let \(c_0, \dots, c_n \in F\) be distinct, and let \(y_0, \dots, y_n \in F\) . Let \(\ell_0, \dots, \ell_n\) be the Lagrange polynomials of the nodes ( @def-lagrange-polynomials-for-nodes ). For all \(i, k \in \{0, \dots, n\}\) , \(\ell_i(c_k) = 1\) if \(k = i\) and \(\ell_i(c_k) = 0\) if \(k \ne i\) . Each \(\ell_i\) has degree exactly \(n\) . The polynomial \(p \coloneqq \sum_{i=0}^{n} y_i \ell_i\) satisfies \(\deg p \le n\) and \(p(c_k) = y_k\) for every \(k\) . It is the only polynomial of degree at most \(n\) with \(p(c_k) = y_k\) for every \(k\) . Every \(q \in F[x]\) with \(\deg q \le n\) satisfies \(q = \sum_{i=0}^{n} q(c_i) \ell_i\) .

title: Theorem 5.5.3 (The Quotient Is a Field Exactly When m Is Irreducible)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(m \in F[x]\) with \(\deg m \ge 1\) . Then \(F[x]/\langle m \rangle\) is a field ( @def-field ) if and only if \(m\) is irreducible over \(F\) ( @def-irreducible-over-field ).

title: Theorem 5.5.2 (The Ring of Polynomials Modulo m)
page: 5.5 Interpolation, Quotient Rings, and the Chinese Remainder Theorem
content: Let \(m \in F[x]\) with \(d \coloneqq \deg m \ge 1\) , and write \([f] = f + \langle m \rangle\) . \(F[x]/\langle m \rangle\) , with \([f] + [g] \coloneqq [f + g]\) and \([f][g] \coloneqq [fg]\) , is a commutative ring with zero \([0]\) and one \([1]\) , and \([1] \ne [0]\) . Each class contains exactly one polynomial of degree less than \(d\) : the remainder of any of its members on division by \(m\) . In particular \(f \equiv g \pmod{m}\) if and only if \(f\) and \(g\) leave the same remainder, and sending each class to its member of degree less than \(d\) is a bijection from \(F[x]/\langle m \rangle\) onto \(\{ r \in F[x] : \deg r < d \}\) . The map \(F \to F[x]/\langle m \rangle\) , \(c \mapsto [c]\) ( \(c\) a constant), is injective and preserves \(+\) and \(\cdot\) . \([f]\) is a unit of \(F[x]/\langle m \rangle\) ( @def-ring-unit ) if and only if \(\gcd(f, m) = 1\) . In that case \([f]^{-1} = [a]\) for any \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \(af + bm = 1\) .

title: Corollary 5.6.7 (Complex Polynomials Split)
content:
Every non-zero \(p \in 
C[x]\) splits over \(
C\) ( @def-splits-over-field ): \(p = a(x - z_1) \cdots (x - z_n)\) with \(n = \deg p\) , \(a\) the leading coefficient of \(p\) , and \(z_1, \dots, z_n \in 
C\) . The multiplicities of the roots of \(p\) add up to \(n\) . The irreducible polynomials of \(
C[x]\) are exactly those of degree \(1\) .

title: Corollary 5.6.9 (The Irreducible Real Polynomials)
content: A polynomial \(p \in \nR[x]\) is irreducible over \(\nR\) if and only if \(\deg p = 1\) , or \(\deg p = 2\) and \(p\) has no real root.

title: Corollary 5.6.11 (Real Polynomials of Odd Degree Have a Real Root)
content: Every \(f \in \nR[x]\) of odd degree has a root in \(\nR\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Find the error)
content:
Here is an argument. Claim. For every non-constant \(p \in 
C[x]\) , \(\abs{p}\) attains a minimum on \(
C\) . Proof. (1) Let \(m \coloneqq \inf \{ \abs{p(z)} : z \in 
C \}\) , which exists since the set is non-empty and bounded below by \(0\) . (2) For each \(k \ge 1\) , pick \(z_k \in

C\) . (5) Then \(\abs{p(z^*)} = \lim \abs{p(z_k)} = m\) . Is the claim true? Does the argument prove it? Name the line that fails and the reason, give a counterexample to the illegal step, and say how the proof in the text avoids it.

content: Let \(m, n \in \nZ_{>0}\) . Prove that \(\gcd(2^m - 1, 2^n - 1) = 2^{\gcd(m, n)} - 1\) in \(\nZ\) .

title: Exercise (R4)
content: Is \(x^4 + x + 1\) irreducible over \(\nF_2\) ?
